To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
for a common class of neural networks, if the number of training examples n is large enough, the mean integrated square error of the network estimator is bounded by the sum of two terms.

the mean squared error of neural network estimation of functions is O(C f(N/(d log N))1/4) with n ~ C f (N/(d log N)1/4) nodes and that this bound is optimal in the order of N and d, up to a logarithmic factor, for a large class of functions.

for neural network estimation the approximation error dominates the estimation error, so the approximation error is the primary consideration, and the approximation error is bounded by the order of the Fourier magnitude of the target function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of a function f(x), where the input variable x is a d-dimensional vector.
the problem of learning a function f from a given set of input/output data pairs (x i, y i) where the function f is assumed to be a member of a class of artificial neural network functions.
the estimation of a target function f by an artificial neural network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mean integrated squared risk of neural network estimation is bounded by a sum of two terms, one that depends on the approximation power of neural networks and one that depends on a complexity measure for the data.

, for the class of networks studied in this paper, a network with a number of nodes that scales with the sample size N in the manner indicated by the analysis can be estimated with a risk that is of the same order as the risk of an optimal series approximation.

the mean integrated squared estimation error for a common class of feedforward neural networks is bounded by $${O}\left( {\frac{{{C_f^2 }}}{n}} \Right) + O(\sqrt {\frac{{{D^2 }n}}{{N}}}\log n)$$ where n, N, d, C f are as above.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the mean integrated squared errors of the networks are bounded by O(C f2/n) and O((ND/n)log n) and the optimal choice for n is C f(N/(Dlog N))1-2.

, in a large class of artificial neural network models, the estimation error can be bounded by O(ND/(Nlog N)) and the approximation error can be bounded in terms of the Fourier transform of the target function.
, for a given architecture, the mean squared error of a network is dominated by the approximation error.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neural networks can be used for nonparametric function estimation with a favorable rate of convergence.
, for moderately large input dimension d and a large number of observations N, the order of approximation error for neural networks is much lower than for series methods.
neural networks are a viable alternative to classical nonparametric methods in high dimensions.
